docs.title: Task & Bug Workflow
docs.text: The full lifecycle of tracked work in gald3r: how tasks and bugs are created, claimed, completed, and verified. Every command on this page was run against this repo's own .gald3r/ while writing it.

docs.title: The state model: SQLite first, Markdown second
docs.text:
.gald3r/gald3r.db is the source of truth for task/bug status transitions. .gald3r/TASKS.md, .gald3r/BUGS.md, and the individual files under .gald3r/tasks/ and .gald3r/bugs/ are a generated, portable cache that a DB write regenerates — never the other way around. If the DB doesn't exist yet (fresh clone, or you've been hand-editing Markdown), gald3r db backfill imports the files into it:

gald3r db backfill

Backfilled 587 task(s), 491 bug(s), 9 document(s), 40 artifact record(s) into
...\.gald3r\gald3r.db.
  Tasks: 587 valid, 0 normalized, 0 skipped, 0 FAILED.
  Bugs:  491 valid, 0 normalized, 0 skipped, 0 FAILED.
  Documents: 9 ingested, 0 skipped.
  Artifact records: 40 valid, 0 normalized, 0 skipped.

(Real output from this repo — 587 tasks and 491 bugs is this project's own multi-month history, not a demo number. A fresh project starts at 0/0.)

Other DB-sync verbs:

gald3r db verify     # report drift between the DB and the .gald3r/ files
gald3r db rebuild     # regenerate the .gald3r/ files FROM the DB (opposite direction of backfill)

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
gald3r task add "Title" -d "Description" --type feature --priority medium

Task types: feature, bug_fix, docs, test, chore, refactor (see gald3r task add --help for the current, authoritative list — it's enforced at creation time, not just a convention). Priority: low / medium / high / critical, or a direct --priority-score 1-10 (see g-rl-35's VALUE rubric — public-facing docs score 6, a release-blocking capability scores 9-10, busywork scores 1).

docs.title: Find what to work on
docs.text:
gald3r task ready

Lists every task that is pending, has no unmet dependencies:, and clears the active value floor — i.e. genuinely pickable right now. gald3r task next narrows that to a single recommendation. gald3r task list shows everything (any status), with the same visual priority-bar chart used everywhere else in the CLI:

tasks[37]{id,display_id,status,indicator,claim_stale,title,milestone,priority,priority_score}:
  "296" | "296" | pending | [📋] | false | T288 Phase 2: remote/entitlement-gated skill-pack marketplace ...
  "574" | "574" | pending | [📋] | false | Validate macOS codesign+notarization pipeline (sign_binary_macos.py) ...
  "557" | "557" | in_progress | [🔄] | true | EPIC: scoped memory subsystem ...
  "555" | "555" | awaiting-verification | [🔍] | false | Egress control: admin-selectable modes ...
  "56"  | "56"  | failed | [❌] | false | P5-B: Pilot platform cutover (one tree) -- GATED

(Trimmed — this repo has 37 non-terminal tasks live at the time of writing. Status indicators: [📋] pending, [🔄] in-progress/claimed, [🔍] awaiting-verification, [✅] completed, [❌] failed, [⏸️] paused, [🚫] cancelled.)

docs.title: Claim and work
docs.text:
gald3r task update T123 --status in-progress

Moves a task from pending to in-progress and records the claim. gald3r claim is the concurrency-safe variant for when multiple agents might grab the same task at once — only one claimant wins.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Every task can carry an acceptance-criteria checklist. Tick items individually as you satisfy them (per-criterion attestation, not a single "done" flag):

gald3r task ac-check T123 --index 1        # tick criterion #1
gald3r task ac-status T123                  # see checked/unchecked status

docs.title: Hand off for review
docs.text: gald3r task update T123 --status awaiting-verification

docs.title: Verify (reviewer side — never the implementer)
docs.text:
gald3r task verify T123 --pass    # -> completed
gald3r task verify T123 --fail    # -> back to pending, with the failure reason recorded

gald3r verify (no task id — the standalone verb) is the completion GATE: it checks whether a task's acceptance criteria are actually satisfied before you call it done, rather than trusting a self-report.

docs.title: Housekeeping
docs.text:
gald3r task regenerate-index    # rebuild TASKS.md from the tasks/**/*.md files
gald3r task-sync-check          # validate TASKS.md against those same files
gald3r task archive              # move completed/failed/cancelled tasks into .gald3r/archive/
gald3r task delete T999          # HARD delete -- only for tasks created in the wrong project
gald3r task release T123         # release a dead/stale claim back to pending

docs.title: Bugs
docs.text:
Bugs mirror the task shape (gald3r bug add/list/show/update/ac-check/archive/delete), with one difference at the terminal state: instead of task verify --pass, a bug is closed with:

gald3r bug add "Title" -d "What's broken" --severity high --file path/to/file.py:42
gald3r bug list
gald3r bug resolve BUG-42

Bug severity uses the same 1-10 damage rubric tasks use for value (see g-rl-35): a typo is a 1-2, a crash on a common path or security gap is 7-8, and secret leaks / data destruction top out at 9-10. gald3r status renders open bugs on the same visual bar chart as tasks, scored by damage instead of value:

Bugs (111 open, 491 all statuses)
  critical  1
  high      1
  medium    15
  low       94

docs.title: Validation and drift
docs.text:
gald3r validate            # schema/status-vocabulary/folder-placement checks on tasks|bugs
gald3r validate --fix      # normalize what's safely auto-fixable
gald3r db verify           # DB-vs-Markdown drift report

gald3r validate runs as a fail-closed pre-commit hook on staged .gald3r/tasks/** and .gald3r/bugs/** in this repo (see .githooks/pre-commit) — a malformed frontmatter field or a task filed under the wrong tasks/<status>/ folder is caught before it merges, not discovered later by a human reading TASKS.md.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• autopilot.md — letting gald3r work the task queue itself instead of running each step by hand
  • cli-reference.md — the full verb catalog, grouped by purpose

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start here whenever gald3r isn't behaving the way you expect. Every output on this page is real, captured while writing it against this repo's own checkout — including the warnings, not just the happy path.

docs.title: Step 1: gald3r doctor
docs.text:
gald3r doctor

gald3r doctor -- <your project dir>
  [OK  ] python       Python 3.13.7 (...\.venv\Scripts\python.exe)
  [OK  ] gald3r_core  gald3r_core 4.0.0
  [WARN] build_fingerprint BUG-433: running binary was built from commit ...,
         but this repo's checked-out source tree ... is currently at commit ....
         This is a REAL commit mismatch (BUG-455 commit-based check) -- ... Fix
         (Task 517): maintainers can run `uv run python
         packaging/maintainer/install_self.py` from this checkout to rebuild
         from source and refresh the PATH binary (BUG-600 -- no longer a
         `gald3r` subcommand).
  [WARN] torch        torch not installed (optional -- only needed for local inference)
  [OK  ] gald3r_home  C:\Users\you\.gald3r_template_core
  [OK  ] providers    ...\providers.yaml: 2 provider(s) configured
  [OK  ] env          set: GALD3R_WORLD_TREE_URL
  [OK  ] identity     project_id=... (your-project-name)
  [OK  ] daemon       no connector lock (Valkyrie not running)
  [OK  ] tel          no .gald3r/tel/ configured yet (optional, T83 epic)
  [OK  ] overlay_freshness no installed overlay found to check (not installed: claude, cursor)
  [OK  ] world_tree   ok
  [WARN] auth         no stored session token (https://api.gald3r.ai)
  [OK  ] channels     no channels.yaml found (channels are optional)

All checks passed (warnings/skips are informational, not blocking).

doctor never fails your session for a WARN — those are informational. Read the specific lines that matter to you:

Line WARN means Fix (if you care) build_fingerprint Your installed binary's build commit doesn't match this checkout's current commit (you edited source after the last build) uv run python packaging/maintainer/install_self.py to rebuild from the current checkout (maintainer-only, BUG-600) torch Local-inference support isn't installed Only needed if you're running models locally through gald3r directly (rare) — most local-model use goes through Ollama/LM Studio instead overlay_freshness An installed platform overlay (.claude/, .cursor/) has drifted from what the CLI would generate today gald3r platform install <platform> --force to resync (see below). gald3r sync --apply is the equivalent for gald3r_core's own contributor checkout specifically — not something most consumer projects use. auth No stored world_tree session token Only needed for team/cross-project features — gald3r login

docs.title: Step 2: gald3r selftest
docs.text:
gald3r selftest

gald3r system test harness -- <project> (gald3r 3.0.0)
Overall: 69% functional (4/7 passing)
  [PARTIAL] Task Management          80%
  [PASS   ] Bug Tracking             100%
  [PASS   ] Git Hooks                100%
  [SKIP   ] Schema Validation        -
  ...
  [FAIL   ] PLATFORM_SPEC            0%
  [FAIL   ] Platform Parity          0%
  ...
Report: <project>\.gald3r\reports\system_test_20260802_000721.md

selftest is a percentage-of-installed-capability check, not a pass/fail gate — a lower number usually means an optional subsystem (platform parity tooling, schema validation) isn't wired up in this particular checkout, not that the CLI is broken. Read the written report file for exactly which sub-checks failed and why.

Known discrepancy (harmless, worth knowing about): selftest's header shows the project's declared gald3r_rel_version from .gald3r/.identity (the framework revision this project's .gald3r/ scaffold was set up against), which can lag behind the actual installed CLI's --version/doctor line — those two numbers answering different questions ("what rel was this project's scaffold built for" vs. "what CLI build is running") is expected, not a sign anything is broken. Run gald3r schema-migrate if you want the project's declared rel brought current.

docs.title: Step 3: gald3r errors / gald3r trace
docs.text:
gald3r errors

No matching error/failure trace records.

(Real output — a clean checkout has none.) When something DID fail during an agent run, errors summarizes it from the trace logs; gald3r trace inspects the full trace log directly for a specific run.

docs.title: Step 4: gald3r medic
docs.text:
gald3r medic --help

usage: gald3r medic [-h] {curate,heal} ...
    curate       Analyze feature/subsystem fragmentation (dry-run) or apply approved moves
    heal         Structural backfill for repos predating a framework feature (dry-run default)

medic diagnoses and repairs problems in your project's .gald3r/ structure itself — broken links, stale indexes, drifted files — fixing what's safe to fix automatically and reporting the rest. Both subcommands default to dry-run; nothing changes on disk until you pass the apply flag they document.

docs.title: Windows: gald3r returns instantly with no output at all (blank exit code)
docs.text:
This was possible before T607 (BUG-650) and is now resolved by the dual-exe split — see below. If you are still hitting it, you're almost certainly invoking gald3rw.exe directly (the GUI-attach binary) from a console-less host, or you have an old, pre-T607 single-binary install still on PATH. Update to the current release (gald3r install update, or re-run gald3r platform install/gald3r sync if you're on an installed overlay) and invoke gald3r, not gald3rw, from a shell.

The two-exe contract (T607): the Windows release ships TWO executables on PATH:

Binary PE subsystem Use it for gald3r.exe Console (3) Terminals, scripts, scheduled tasks, AI-agent shells — anywhere you type gald3r yourself or a script invokes it directly. Always waits, always prints, always returns a real exit code — including from a console-less PowerShell host. gald3rw.exe GUI (2), attach Throne, IDE hooks, the valk daemon, and any other spawn from a process that must never flash a console window (the BUG-556 fix). Interactive terminal usage still prints normally; a console-less parent gets zero console flash and no output — by design, since nothing is watching for it there.

Before T607, only one binary existed and it was built GUI-subsystem (gald3rw.exe's shape today) — every direct terminal/agent/automation invocation on Windows had this exact "returns instantly with no output" failure mode. That binary is retired; gald3r on a current install is console-subsystem and does not have this problem.

If you are deliberately invoking gald3rw.exe yourself (uncommon — it exists for programmatic/GUI-parented spawns, not interactive use) and want its output anyway, any of these forms works:

cmd /c "gald3rw --version"          # cmd allocates a console; output flows normally

Start-Process gald3rw -ArgumentList "--version" -NoNewWindow -Wait `
  -RedirectStandardOutput out.txt   # explicit handles bypass console attachment

Normal interactive terminals (Windows Terminal, VS Code/Cursor terminal panels, cmd.exe, Git Bash), Python subprocess captures, and CI runners are unaffected either way. If you hit this from source (uv install), uv run gald3r ... is also unaffected — it runs the console-subsystem Python entry point directly, never a compiled binary.

docs.title: "gald3r: command not found" / binary not on PATH
docs.text: You installed via uv sync but didn't add .venv\Scripts (Windows) / .venv/bin (macOS/Linux) to PATH, or you edited PATH in a terminal that was already open. See install.md — and fully restart your terminal/IDE after any PATH edit.

docs.title: Installed platform overlay (.claude/, .cursor/) looks stale or hooks aren't firing
docs.text:
gald3r doctor

[WARN] overlay_freshness DRIFT -- claude: 1 file(s) changed (.claude/settings.json) |
       Run `uv run gald3r sync --apply` (or `uv run gald3r platform install <platform>
       --force`) to resync the installed overlay from the live neutral_source/ tree. ...

(Real output, trimmed.) This is the platform-overlay analog of the build_fingerprint check above — the files actually on disk in .claude//.cursor/ no longer match what gald3r platform install would generate today (you hand-edited an installed file, or the generator changed since you last installed). Fix:

gald3r platform install claude --into . --force

--force overwrites the drifted files with a fresh render — including a fresh, non-destructive .claude/settings.json merge (see install.md), so your own mcpServers/permissions/other top-level keys survive even across a forced resync.

docs.title: gald3r status says "No .gald3r/gald3r.db found yet"
docs.text:
Expected on a fresh checkout, or after cloning a repo where the DB (gitignored by design — it's a regeneratable cache, not source of truth for the files) wasn't carried over:

gald3r db backfill

rebuilds it from the .gald3r/tasks/ and .gald3r/bugs/ files. See task-bug-workflow.md.

docs.title: A task/bug file won't pass gald3r validate
docs.text:
gald3r validate --fix

normalizes whatever's safely auto-fixable (missing-but-inferable frontmatter fields, wrong tasks/<status>/ folder placement for the declared status). Anything it can't safely fix on its own, it reports instead of guessing.

docs.title: An autopilot/swarm run looks stuck
docs.text:
gald3r go-status

Read-only check on whether a running autopilot loop is ALIVE, IDLE-WAIT, STALLED, or STOPPED — without interrupting it. See autopilot.md for the rest of the run-management verbs (autopilot stop, worktree steer/queue).

docs.title: gald3r login says the server "does not yet expose device-code auth"
docs.text:
gald3r login

gald3r login: world_tree does not yet expose device-code auth (404 on POST /api/v1/auth/device/code). Use `gald3r login --token <token>` instead.

(Real output.) gald3r login with no arguments starts an interactive device-code sign-in: it requests a code from world_tree, prints a verification URL plus a short code for you to enter in any browser, polls until you approve, and stores the resulting session token — no raw JWT handling needed. The message above is the honest fail-closed path while the deployed world_tree server predates those auth routes: until the server ships them, use a pre-issued Bearer token instead:

gald3r login --token <TOKEN>                              # one-off
gald3r login --token <TOKEN> --base-url https://api.gald3r.ai   # explicit API base (default shown)

$GALD3R_WORLD_TREE_TOKEN is the equivalent env-var form, useful in CI or so you don't have to pass --token by hand every time. gald3r logout clears whatever session is currently stored (gald3r logout: no stored session to clear if there wasn't one — also not an error). None of this is required for local, single-project use — see the auth line in Step 1 above: a missing token is a WARN, never a blocking failure, and only matters once you're using world_tree-backed features (valk, cross-project workspace sync, version-check's online path). See coordination.md for what those features actually unlock.

docs.title: Cross-project coordination looks out of sync
docs.text:
gald3r workspace status
gald3r workspace pull

See coordination.md for the full WPAC/Valkyrie model — most drift is resolved by a pull reconciling the local mirror against the online registry.

Commands are the slash-command layer of CRASH -- what you actually type in an AI IDE (/g-<name> in Claude Code, @g-<name> in Cursor and most of the rest of the supported roster) to dispatch a piece of gald3r's workflow. Every command below is a thin, generated dispatcher onto a skill; the description, arguments, and grouping come straight from that command's own frontmatter -- nothing here is hand-guessed.

192 commands total.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Creating, updating, and tracking work in .gald3r/tasks/.

  • /g-go -- Two-phase pipeline: implement tasks/bugs, then auto-spawn a fresh independent reviewer (optional swarm mode).
  • /g-go-code -- Implement queued tasks/bugs through to awaiting-verification only; never runs review itself
  • /g-go-code-swarm -- Alias for g-go-code --swarm: implementation-only swarm that partitions tasks into parallel coding buckets
  • /g-go-go -- Autopilot loop: rolling g-go-code-swarm + g-go-review-swarm cycles across the workspace until a hard stop
  • /g-go-review -- Verify tasks/bugs awaiting review in a fresh session: PASS/FAIL scoring, no self-review, auto-commits verdict.
  • /g-go-review-swarm -- Run g-go-review verification in parallel across M reviewer agents on the review queue (round-robin).
  • /g-go-swarm -- Run the full g-go pipeline (implement then auto-review) in swarm mode across parallel Phase 1/2 agents.
  • /g-grooming -- Deprecated stub
  • /g-juggernaut -- Alias for g-mission
  • /g-kamikaze -- Alias for g-mission
  • /g-mission -- Run an autonomous g-go-go loop until a stated condition is met, optionally draining the queue.
  • /g-propose -- Generate a proposal doc (design, PRD draft, task breakdown) from a feature description
  • /g-pt -- List, switch, copy, or validate gald3r workflow profiles (project types) via gald3r project-type
  • /g-queue -- Append a follow-up prompt to a running g-go-code worktree's queue.md, or list pending items
  • /g-report -- Generate a backlog status report: last commit, available/in-progress/blocked tasks, recommendations
  • /g-steer -- Inject a one-shot steering prompt into a running g-go-code worktree session via steer.md.
  • /g-task-add -- Create a new task (ID, complexity score, file, TASKS.md entry) via g-skl-tasks CREATE TASK.
  • /g-task-archive -- Archive completed/failed/cancelled tasks into .gald3r/archive/ buckets via gald3r task archive (T497).
  • /g-task-del -- Hard-delete a mis-routed task via git rm + commit, per g-rl-33 Routing Error Hard Delete (gald3r task delete, T497).
  • /g-task-new -- Deprecated alias for @g-task-add
  • /g-task-sync-check -- Validate TASKS.md matches the tasks/ files, catching phantom or orphaned task entries.
  • /g-task-upd -- Update a task's status, priority, dependencies, promotion/demotion, or release-hold fields.
  • /g-task-update -- Deprecated alias for @g-task-upd
  • /g-wishlist-mine -- Mine a human-prose wishlist doc into gald3r tasks via g-skl-wishlist-mine, read-only against the doc

docs.title: Bugs & Quality
docs.text:
Reporting, fixing, and archiving defects; QA workflows.

  • /g-bug-add -- Report a new bug via g-skl-bugs REPORT
  • /g-bug-archive -- Move resolved/closed bugs out of BUGS.md into count-bucketed .gald3r/archive/ history via gald3r bug archive (T497).
  • /g-bug-del -- Hard-delete a mis-routed bug via git rm + commit, per g-rl-33 Routing Error Hard Delete (gald3r bug delete, T497).
  • /g-bug-fix -- Fix a specified bug by BUG-NNN id via the g-bugs FIX BUG operation.
  • /g-bug-report -- Deprecated alias for g-bug-add
  • /g-bug-upd -- Update a bug record field (status, severity, note, workspace-repos) via g-skl-bugs UPDATE BUG.
  • /g-code-review -- Run a depth-scaled code review (Quick/Standard/Comprehensive) on given files, a PR, or recent git changes.
  • /g-dependency-graph -- Generate or refresh task and/or subsystem dependency Mermaid graphs via g-skl-dependency-graph.
  • /g-doctor -- Run gald3r environment health checks (identity, tasks, MCP, vault, platform parity, skills quality) with safe auto-fixes.
  • /g-go-bugs -- Two-phase pipeline: reproduce and fix open bugs, then an independent reviewer agent verifies each fix
  • /g-go-bugs-swarm -- Parallel swarm variant of g-go-bugs: partitions open bugs into buckets, fixes then reviews them concurrently
  • /g-hotfix-open -- Branch a hotfix from the latest release tag, scaffold a hotfix task + worktree, optionally open a Draft PR.
  • /g-qa -- Activate the QA system for bug tracking, bug-task linking, and retroactive fix documentation
  • /g-review -- Deprecated alias
  • /g-skill-review -- List, review, promote, or discard auto-proposed skill drafts from g-go-review --propose-skill.
  • /g-swot-review -- Run a 5-pass SWOT analysis on the current project phase and write a report to .gald3r/logs/swot/.
  • /g-test -- Create, audit, run, or gate L1/L2/L3 test plans for a subsystem/feature via g-skl-test.
  • /g-triage -- Parse pasted email/Slack/notes/URLs, classify into IDEA/BUG/TASK/INFO, then write after approval

docs.title: Pipelines & Autopilot (the g-go family)
docs.text:
Implement/review pipelines, swarms, autopilot loops, and agent hiring.

  • /g-agent-hire -- Hire a new gald3r agent through a 4-phase research-gated workflow: research, draft, review, hire.
  • /g-go-status -- Report whether an active g-go-go autopilot run is ALIVE, IDLE-WAIT, STALLED, or STOPPED (read-only).
  • /g-go-xreview -- Review queue via a different-vendor reviewer (g-skl-cross-review): diff-only, gates-first, never-merge.

docs.text:

  • /g-cleanup -- Deprecated
  • /g-command-new -- Scaffold a new slash command file into a chosen platform folder or repo path with prompted metadata.
  • /g-constraint-add -- Add a new architectural constraint to CONSTRAINTS.md via g-skl-constraints ADD operation.
  • /g-constraint-check -- Validate the current task/implementation against active CONSTRAINTS.md rules via g-skl-constraints CHECK.
  • /g-constraint-del -- Deprecate a constraint in CONSTRAINTS.md (keeps audit trail) via g-skl-constraints DEPRECATE operation.
  • /g-constraint-upd -- Edit an existing constraint definition in CONSTRAINTS.md via g-skl-constraints UPDATE operation.
  • /g-curator -- Audit and grade all SKILL.md files via g-skl-curator, proposing merge/archive candidates (never deletes).
  • /g-dec -- Present the outstanding OWNER decisions
  • /g-goal -- Set, view, or clear a persistent session goal (ACTIVE_GOAL.md) with turn-budget drift correction for g-go.
  • /g-goal-update -- Update the Goals section of PROJECT.md via g-project UPDATE PROJECT.MD operation.
  • /g-idea-capture -- Capture an idea into IDEA_BOARD.md via g-ideas CAPTURE, without derailing the current session.
  • /g-idea-farm -- Scan the codebase in 5 passes, adding up to 10 new deduplicated ideas to IDEA_BOARD.md via g-ideas FARM.
  • /g-idea-review -- List active IDEA_BOARD.md ideas and prompt to promote, shelve, or keep each via g-ideas REVIEW.
  • /g-medic -- Run tiered L1-L4 .gald3r/ health diagnostics and heals via the g-medic skill.
  • /g-medkit -- Deprecated alias that delegates to @g-medic for tiered .gald3r/ health diagnostics.
  • /g-migrate -- Scan and rewrite callers of a skill or API interface to match a new interface signature.
  • /g-rule-new -- Scaffold a new project rule file in your chosen platform folder or repo location
  • /g-setup -- Initialize or reinitialize the gald3r v3 task-management system in this project via g-skl-setup.
  • /g-skill-new -- Scaffold a new SKILL.md for your project in a chosen platform folder or custom repo path.
  • /g-status -- Generate a project status report
  • /g-subsystem-add -- Create a new subsystem spec file and SUBSYSTEMS.md entry via g-skl-subsystems CREATE SUBSYSTEM SPEC.
  • /g-subsystem-audit -- Audit subsystem and skill group-tagging compliance against PRODUCT_SYSTEMS.md via g-skl-subsystems AUDIT.
  • /g-subsystem-del -- Mark a subsystem deprecated in its spec and SUBSYSTEMS.md via g-skl-subsystems DEPRECATE SUBSYSTEM.
  • /g-subsystem-graph -- Rebuild .gald3r/SUBSYSTEM_GRAPH.md: subsystem dependency edges, layer analysis, circular-dependency detection.
  • /g-subsystem-upd -- Update a subsystem spec's status, dependencies, or locations and append an Activity Log entry.
  • /g-subsystems -- Sync-check subsystems against SUBSYSTEMS.md, or list active/all subsystems with --status.
  • /g-system-rebuild -- Regenerate PRODUCT_SYSTEMS.md by scanning SKILL.md subsystem_memberships and parent_system tags.
  • /g-update -- Check or apply gald3r framework version updates via --check/--apply/--changelog/--dry-run flags
  • /g-upgrade -- Check for gald3r updates and upgrade if available

docs.title: WPAC & Workspace Coordination
docs.text:
Cross-project topology, inbox triage, broadcasts, and Workspace-Control.

  • /g-valk-ask -- Ask another project a grounded, cited question via Valkyrie (gald3r valk ask), queuing if offline
  • /g-valk-connect -- Set or verify this repo's Valkyrie connector base URL and login token against world_tree
  • /g-valk-inquire -- Stream a grounded, cited answer from a project's context via Valkyrie SSE ask/stream route
  • /g-valk-list -- List every registered Valkyrie world_tree connector on this machine via gald3r valk list
  • /g-valk-messages -- List the durable Valkyrie events ledger (notifications, asks, inquiries) via gald3r valk messages
  • /g-valk-start -- Start the Valkyrie world_tree connector, optionally detached as a resident sync process
  • /g-valk-status -- Check whether this project's Valkyrie world_tree connector is currently running (read-only)
  • /g-valk-stop -- Stop the running Valkyrie world_tree connector for this project and clear its lock
  • /g-valk-sync -- Flush every queued Valkyrie outbox entry to world_tree (reconcile-on-reconnect up-sync)
  • /g-workspace-export -- Dry-run plan of a Workspace-Control export via g-skl-workspace EXPORT PLAN; alias for g-wrkspc-export
  • /g-workspace-status -- Show read-only Workspace-Control status via g-skl-workspace STATUS; alias for g-wrkspc-status
  • /g-workspace-sync -- Preview a Workspace-Control manifest sync dry-run via g-skl-workspace SYNC PLAN (alias for g-wrkspc-sync).
  • /g-workspace-validate -- Validate the Workspace-Control manifest and task/bug routing metadata via g-skl-workspace VALIDATE.
  • /g-wpac-adopt -- Adopt a target project as this project's WPAC child, updating link_topology.md on both sides.
  • /g-wpac-archive-inbox -- Archive stale [DONE]/[RESOLVED] WPAC inbox messages older than a day threshold and prune INBOX.md.
  • /g-wpac-ask -- Send a WPAC REQUEST to the parent project's INBOX and mark the blocked local task.
  • /g-wpac-claim -- Claim a target project as this project's WPAC parent, updating link_topology.md on both sides.
  • /g-wpac-move -- Move files or subsystems to a related WPAC project with provenance logging and safety gates.
  • /g-wpac-notify -- Send a lightweight [INFO] notification to one or more project INBOXes
  • /g-wpac-order -- Broadcast a WPAC task order from this parent project to one or more child projects.
  • /g-wpac-promote -- Promote a Workspace-Control controlled_member repo to a fully self-managed autonomous_child.
  • /g-wpac-read -- Triage and action the WPAC INBOX
  • /g-wpac-send-to -- Send files, features, specs, ideas, bugs, or code to a related WPAC project with INBOX notification.
  • /g-wpac-spawn -- Spawn a new gald3r project seeded from this one, with full setup and bidirectional WPAC topology linking.
  • /g-wpac-status -- Show full WPAC status
  • /g-wpac-sync -- Sync contract changes with sibling project(s) via WPAC INBOX using g-skl-wpac-sync (advisory only)
  • /g-wrkspc -- Dispatch to Workspace-Control subcommands (status/validate/member-list/init/spawn/etc.) via g-skl-workspace
  • /g-wrkspc-adopt -- Adopt an existing populated gald3r project into Workspace-Control via g-skl-workspace ADOPT
  • /g-wrkspc-export -- Dry-run plan a Workspace-Control export of manifest members via g-skl-workspace EXPORT_PLAN
  • /g-wrkspc-init -- Create or promote the Workspace-Control manifest via g-skl-workspace INIT_PLAN/INIT_APPLY
  • /g-wrkspc-member-add -- Register a repo as a Workspace-Control manifest member via g-skl-workspace MEMBER_ADD_PLAN/APPLY
  • /g-wrkspc-member-list -- List repositories declared in the Workspace-Control manifest via g-skl-workspace MEMBER_LIST
  • /g-wrkspc-member-remove -- Plan or apply removal/retirement of a Workspace-Control manifest member via g-skl-workspace MEMBER_REMOVE
  • /g-wrkspc-spawn -- Spawn a new local Workspace-Control member project and register it via g-skl-workspace SPAWN_PLAN/APPLY
  • /g-wrkspc-status -- Show Workspace-Control manifest status (owner, members, lifecycle, git state) via g-skl-workspace STATUS
  • /g-wrkspc-sync -- Dry-run plan a Workspace-Control member alignment check via g-skl-workspace SYNC_PLAN
  • /g-wrkspc-validate -- Validate the Workspace-Control manifest and routing metadata via g-skl-workspace VALIDATE

docs.title: Release & Versioning
docs.text:
CHANGELOG promotion, release records, ROADMAP, ship/ hotfix flow.

  • /g-feat-add -- Stage a new feature in features/ via g-skl-features STAGE, deduping against existing features first.
  • /g-feat-del -- Archive a feature staging doc via g-skl-features ARCHIVE FEATURE, moving it to features/archive/
  • /g-feat-new -- Deprecated alias for g-feat-add; stage a new feature via g-skl-features STAGE (status: staging)
  • /g-feat-promote -- Promote a specced feature to committed via g-skl-features PROMOTE, interactively creating tasks
  • /g-feat-rename -- Rename a feature's slug and title via g-skl-features RENAME, updating file, YAML, and index
  • /g-feat-upd -- Update a feature staging doc's YAML fields and FEATURES.md index row via g-skl-features UPDATE FEATURE
  • /g-install-agent -- DEPRECATED alias for /g-install-update
  • /g-install-throne -- Download, verify (minisign), and stage the Gald3r Throne installer from the latest GitHub release.
  • /g-install-update -- Download, verify, and install the latest signed gald3r_core release, replacing whatever gald3r currently resolves to on PATH.
  • /g-plan -- Guide creation of PLAN.md, PROJECT.md, and SUBSYSTEMS.md via the gald3r planning workflow.
  • /g-pr-close -- Merge a PASSed GitHub PR via g-skl-github-pr READY/COMMENT/CLOSE, or leave FAILed PRs as Draft
  • /g-pr-open -- Open a Draft GitHub PR for the active task via g-skl-github-pr OPEN, with stacked-PR routing
  • /g-prd-add -- Create a new PRD draft file via g-skl-prds CREATE, with tier/framework/classification flags
  • /g-prd-del -- Soft-delete a PRD via g-skl-prds ARCHIVE, moving it to prds/archive/ and updating PRDS.md
  • /g-prd-revise -- Revise a released PRD via g-skl-prds REVISE, creating a new draft that supersedes it
  • /g-prd-upd -- Update a PRD field (status, authorizer, framework, risk) via g-skl-prds UPDATE
  • /g-release-accelerate -- Pull a release's target date earlier, cascading the delta to later planned releases (g-skl-release ACCELERATE)
  • /g-release-assign -- Assign task IDs to a release, updating its tasks list and RELEASES.md (g-skl-release ASSIGN)
  • /g-release-new -- Create a new release file and RELEASES.md row with an auto-computed target date (g-skl-release CREATE)
  • /g-release-propose -- Analyze completed tasks and propose the next semantic version bump + draft release notes.
  • /g-release-publish -- Regenerate ROADMAP.md from all planned/in-progress/released release files (g-skl-release PUBLISH)
  • /g-release-status -- Show release status summary or per-release task/blocker detail (g-skl-release STATUS)
  • /g-ship -- Promote [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entries to a versioned release via g-skl-ship (major/minor/patch/status).

docs.title: Vault & Research
docs.text:
The file-first knowledge vault, recon/ingest, and clean-room rewrites.

  • /g-issue-sync -- Two-way sync gald3r tasks with GitHub Issues via g-skl-github-pr (pull, push, or update per task).
  • /g-recon-docs -- Capture a docs URL into the vault with periodic staleness tracking via g-skl-recon-docs
  • /g-recon-file -- Capture a local file (PDF/DOCX/XLSX/etc.) into the vault knowledge store via g-skl-recon-file
  • /g-recon-repo -- Capture a GitHub repo into the vault as a structured note via g-skl-recon-repo (--deep for full analysis)
  • /g-recon-url -- Capture a URL into vault research/articles/ as a one-time snapshot via g-skl-recon-url (--deep for analysis)
  • /g-recon-yt -- Capture a YouTube video transcript into the vault via g-skl-recon-yt (--deep for full analysis)
  • /g-res-apply -- Convert approved recon-report features into gald3r goals, features, subsystems, and tasks (g-skl-res-apply)
  • /g-res-deep -- Deep analysis of a captured repo, URL, or vault note
  • /g-res-review -- Review recon reports and triage unadopted features for approve/reject/defer (g-skl-res-review)
  • /g-vault-frontmatter-fix -- Retrofit missing Obsidian YAML frontmatter onto vault notes; dry-run by default, backs up files on --apply
  • /g-vault-ingest -- Route new knowledge into the file-first vault with Obsidian-safe wikilinks via g-skl-vault ingest
  • /g-vault-lint -- Audit the vault for freshness, broken wikilinks, orphan pages, and OKF-conformance via gald3r vault lint
  • /g-vault-process-inbox -- Route dropped files in the vault raw/ inbox to research notes, URL/YouTube ingest, or raw/failed/
  • /g-vault-search -- Search the file-first vault's index.md and _index.yaml notes and answer from matched entries
  • /g-vault-status -- Summarize vault health: note counts by type, active paths, recent log.md activity, migration warnings

docs.title: CRASH Reference: Hooks
docs.text:
GENERATED FILE -- do not hand-edit. Produced from every item under src/gald3r_core/platform/pipeline/neutral_source/hooks/ by gald3r platform crash-reference. To regenerate: uv run gald3r platform crash-reference --apply.

Hooks are the one CRASH type that is real, executing code -- plain scripts (mostly .py) wired into your IDE's lifecycle events (session start, pre-tool-call, stop, ...) by a platform-specific registration file. You do not invoke a hook by name; it fires automatically when its registered event happens. This page documents what each hook does and when it fires -- never its internal implementation.

38 hooks total.

A skill (SKILL.md) is the actual instruction package a command hands off to -- commands themselves are thin dispatchers. A skill loads either because a command invoked it, or because your agent's own judgment matched its frontmatter description: field without you typing a slash command at all. You never hand-edit a skill's local copy; behavior changes land upstream in neutral_source/ and arrive on your next platform install/update.
